utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case number IT-97-25-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. For the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: If it please the Court. Dirk Ryneveld, and with me today is my colleague, Peggy Kuo, and our case manager, George Huber for the Prosecution. We're prepared to proceed today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, Your Honour, the Defence will be represented by legal counsellor, Miroslav Vasic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic. The accused, are you able to understand the proceedings in a language which you know?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, it's a fairly general practice in the Tribunal that when an indictment is presented or an amended indictment is presented, the accused waives the reading of it in full. Have you discussed this particular matter with your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the accused has been served with the amended indictment. He has understood it, he is ready to plead, and there is no need for us to read the indictment, only perhaps the counts on which he is asked to plead. So there is no need to read the indictment in full.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Krnojelac, I propose to take each of these counts and ask you how you plead to each. Your answer to each should be either "guilty" or "not guilty," as the case may be. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on the 18th of June, 1998, I pleaded on this same indictment, as far as I understand, judicial affairs. So I think it would be sufficient for me to plead again, 15 months later, on the same counts. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. In relation to the first count, a crime against humanity, based upon persecution on political, racial, and/or religious grounds, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The second count, a crime against humanity, based upon torture. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 3, a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions, based upon torture. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 4, a violation of the laws or customs of war, based again upon torture. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 5, a crime against humanity, based upon inhumane acts. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 6, a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions, based upon wilfully causing serious injury to body or health. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 7, a violation of the laws or customs of war, based upon cruel treatment. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 8, a crime against humanity, based upon murder. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 9, a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions, based upon wilful killing. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 10, a violation of the laws or customs of war, based upon murder. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 11, a crime against humanity, based upon imprisonment. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 12, a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions, based upon unlawful confinement of a civilian. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 13, a crime against humanity, based upon inhumane acts. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 14, a grave breach, based upon wilfully causing great suffering. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 15, a violation of the laws or customs of war, based upon cruel treatment. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 16, a crime against humanity, based upon enslavement. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Count 17, a grave breach, based upon inhumane treatment. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And Count 18, a violation of the laws or customs of war, based upon slavery. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krnojelac. Would you sit down, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There has been a motion filed by the accused for an extension of time within which to file a Rule 72 motion. Mr. Vasic, following the procedure adopted today, or having your client plead to the amended indictment, you now have a time limit provided by Rule 50(C). You have a further period of 30 days within which to file any preliminary motions, pursuant to Rule 72. So you would not need to proceed with your motion, I'd suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is there any problem from the Prosecution's point of view if I simply note that the motion has not been proceeded with?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: None whatsoever. That's perfectly in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.
